Priya M.: Thanks for the all-hands today — quick follow-up on engineering process items: are we standardizing on a 3-week sprint cadence for product+infra work?
Sam H.: Short answer: not hard-locked. We want more predictable planning windows, so teams should aim for 3-week cycles where it reduces context switching, but teams can stay at 2 or 4 if it suits their flow. The goal is consistency across product areas, not forced uniformity.
Jules K.: Clarify oncall implications — if cadence changes, will rotation windows change too?
Sam H.: Good call. We're shifting primary oncall to 7-day rotations (Mon-Sun) to reduce handoff friction, with the same secondary overnight/holiday split. This means fewer handovers per quarter.
Aria L.: Any update to the paging policy or escalation times?
Sam H.: Escalation stays the same: sev1 pages immediate, 15-min SLA for ack, 30-min for mitigation plan. We are revising the runbook templates to make the 15/30 targets more actionable (clear checklist items).
Ken P.: For Dedicated customers and SLAs, what are the hard latency targets we support?
Sam H.: For Dedicated standard profiles: p95 <= 250ms for common gen models. For long-context and specialized models we'll publish profile-specific targets (e.g., p95 <= 700ms for 64k context). SLA exceptions will be documented per model.
Lina S.: How are quality bars enforced for model rollouts?
Sam H.: New guardrails: every model rollout needs a prerelease eval harness (baseline prompts + expected metrics). We enforce a "no-regression" gate on embeddings similarity and generation toxicity. Rollouts also require a canary stage with automated metric checks.
Priya M.: Can you paste the approved canary config we discussed?
Sam H.: Sure — example we'll use as default rollout template: 
```json
{"rollout": {"canary_percent": 5, "stages": [5,25,100], "health_metrics": ["p95_latency","error_rate","quality_regressions"], "auto_promote_on": "all_checks_green"}}
```
Jules K.: Do we have automation to promote if checks are green?
Sam H.: Yes — CI/CD will auto-promote after 2 consecutive green evaluations and no new errors for 30m. Ops can abort via the deployment dashboard.
Aria L.: Who owns updating the runbooks and checklists?
Jules K.: I'll take runbooks. Aria offered to own the post-release checklist and the eval prompt sets.
Ken P.: I'll coordinate the SLA communications to customers and update the status pages.
Priya M.: Action items: Sam to update the rollout template in the repo, Jules to refresh runbook, Aria to publish eval sets, Ken to update customer-facing SLA doc. Please drop PR links in #eng-process when ready. :thumbsup: 
deploy-bot: Deployment started for release/infra-2026-03 at 2112345800 :rocket:
Lina S.: Noted — any temporary changes to the blameless-postmortem timing?
Sam H.: No change — standard PM window remains: 72h incident initial summary, 7-day followup with RCA. We will add a quick "post-deploy health check" at 2h and 24h after major rollouts.
Priya M.: Awesome. Thanks everyone — let's keep this thread for short updates and move docs to #eng-process.
Jules K.: +1, will post the runbook PR today.
Aria L.: I'll post the eval harness by EOD tomorrow.
Ken P.: I'll send a draft SLA blurb for review.
Priya M.: Thanks — leadership will review progress in next week sync. :white_check_mark:
